brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer at the specified corner of the specified cell
requirements.evidence: drawer:0#0,0#cut on piece:0,0,0;half-n at q0 r0, installed on its cut face (southern edge).

requirements.requirement: One spike at the very same corner of the same cell, touching the drawer
requirements.evidence: Configurator enforces SPIKE_CLASH: spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 stands at a corner this drawer fills. Attempting addSpike at junction [0,0|0,1|1,0] with drawer present was refused with SPIKE_CLASH (also tried variant stud). The configurator offers only a different junction, e.g. [0,1|1,0|1,1] after adding piece 1,1,0. Same-corner co-location is prohibited by placement rules and mesh clash.

finish.summary: Built the half-n base at 0,0,0 with drawer on its cut face to satisfy the drawer-at-corner requirement. The second half of the request—spike touching the drawer at the exact same three-base junction [0,0|0,1|1,0]—is blocked by configurator rule SPIKE_CLASH. All direct placements were refused, confirming the geometry is not allowed. Build capped and locked, mesh clear.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

result.note: A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base first. Half-n and half-s take any drawer style; half-e and half-w take a slide, swing or long drawer (find_sockets offers those once the half base is on). No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
